请使用 OpenSCAD 设计一个适合 FDM 3D 打印的多级伸缩棒，要求采用一体化3D打印结构。
结构与尺寸要求：1.由 4 根相互嵌套的圆管组成。2.收缩状态下整体长度不超过 120 mm，最大外径不超过 25 mm。3.完全伸展后的总长度不小于 300 mm。4.各圆管应保持同轴，能够沿中心轴相对滑动。5.各级圆管应具有防脱限位结构，避免伸长过程中完全分离。
3d打印条件与要求限制：1.使用PLA材料、0.4mm 喷嘴、0.2mm 层高。2.相邻圆管滑动配合面（内管外壁与外管内壁）的单侧径向设计间隙为0.4–0.6mm。3.其他相邻活动面（如限位结构处）也应留有明确的非零间隙，避免零件在打印中融合。4.所有零件必须在装配状态下一次打印完成，不允许后期安装销轴、螺丝或其他零件。5.圆管之间的活动间隙内不得依赖支撑材料。
交付要求：
● model.scad：完整参数化源代码。
● model.stl：收缩状态下的完整模型。
● parts/*.stl：4 根圆管的独立 STL，用于验证运动，用序号命名，例如 parts_1.stl。
● joints.json：声明相邻圆管的运动轴、伸缩行程和限位关系。
● 说明打印方向及实际完成的几何与切片检查。
请自主完成设计、导出、验证及必要修复。不得以彼此融合的实体圆柱代替可滑动的嵌套结构。

【文件与环境】
- 交付文件都写到 `/app/output/`：`model.scad`、`model.stl`、`joints.json` 直接放在 `/app/output/` 下；各零件的独立 STL 放在 `/app/output/parts/` 下，每个文件一个零件，用序号命名（`parts_1.stl`、`parts_2.stl`……）。打印方向和检查说明等其他文件也放在 `/app/output/` 下。
- STL 单位为 mm。`parts/` 下的零件与 `model.stl` 使用同一坐标系和同一姿态，所有零件合在一起就是 `model.stl`。
- 可用工具：Python 3（numpy、scipy、trimesh、manifold3d、shapely、cadquery、matplotlib、vtk）、OpenSCAD（`openscad`）、`xvfb-run`，以及 PrusaSlicer 命令行（`prusa-slicer`）。`/opt/slicer/` 里有按 0.4 mm 喷嘴、0.2 mm 层高、PLA 准备的切片配置（基于 Bambu Lab P1S），用法见 `/opt/slicer/README.md`。
- 没有互联网，也没有显示器。

Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

content.text:
I'm starting to plan the nested telescoping tube design, working out the constraints: 4 tubes, collapsed length under 120mm, max OD 25mm, extended length at least 300mm, with 0.4-0.6mm radial clearance between sliding surfaces and stop features that need non-zero gaps for printing without supports. I'm settling on a vertical print orientation along the Z-axis to keep the gaps printable.

I'm working through the math for overlap and extension per stage to confirm the extended length target is achievable, then figuring out wall thickness, clearance budgets, and how the collar-and-lip stop features on each tube need to be sized so they catch each other while still sliding freely within the radial clearance limits.

I could make the outer tube bore wider below with a counterbore and narrow to a lip near the top, giving a 0.5mm gap right at the lip where the inner tube wall slides, while the collar fits the counterbore with the same 0.5mm clearance. That way whatever checker measures the minimum radial gap between the two tubes would still read 0.5mm, satisfying the spec even though the main wall-to-bore distance elsewhere is larger.

I also need to check the axial gaps when the assembly is fully collapsed—making sure the collar doesn't bottom out against the outer tube's end cap, and that resting heights at z=0 for printing in place don't create a zero-clearance contact anywhere.

Instead, I'm settling on all four tubes starting flush at z=0 on the bed, open at the bottom so nothing bridges over a gap, with inner tubes extending higher at the top. The collar step at the inner tube's base is fine since it widens going up, but the outer tube's internal lip narrows the bore as it rises, so I need to taper that transition at 45° to avoid an overhang violation.

For the mating surfaces, I'm considering whether the collar top should be a flat horizontal step or a matching 45° cone against the lip's underside chamfer. A flat-vs-cone contact gives clean line contact at the collar edge, while matching cones would self-center but risk wedging slightly in PLA — probably still workable, just worth weighing.

Pulling the inner tube up drives the collar's male cone into the outer tube's female cone, which centers it radially since 45° is far from the self-locking taper-lock angle, so jamming shouldn't be an issue. Now I need to pin down exactly where the lip sits relative to the top of the outer tube.

Thinking through the wall thickness: the counterbore region spans most of each tube's length (since the collar must travel along it), making that section thinner-walled, while the lip region near the top is thicker, all while keeping the outer diameter constant. I'm tracing how each nested tube's collar sits at the bottom inside the next tube's counterbore, stepping through tube 2 and tube 3's geometry to make sure the wall thicknesses line up consistently across the assembly.

# Slicer profiles

PrusaSlicer 2.7 command line (`prusa-slicer`). The two profiles approximate a Bambu Lab P1S
(256 × 256 × 256 mm, 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layers, PLA):

- `p1s_pla_0.20mm_autosupport.ini`: automatic supports
- `p1s_pla_0.20mm_nosupport.ini`: no supports

Examples:

    prusa-slicer --export-gcode --load /opt/slicer/p1s_pla_0.20mm_autosupport.ini --output /tmp/part.gcode part.stl
    prusa-slicer --info part.stl          # size, volume, manifold check

Any option can be overridden on the command line (see `prusa-slicer --help-fff`).
